summary: edge slow-start causes final stream segment omission on large streaming responses
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on BrightCart report that long streaming responses (multiple kilobyte final paragraphs) occasionally end without the final segment (last 1-3 sentences) — the stream connection terminates and the client does not receive the concluding text or the terminal event. This appears to happen only for large responses (8k+ tokens in aggregate) and is intermittent (~0.5% of streams during peak).

Impact:
- BrightCart critical customer-facing chat flows missing concluding instructions, causing UX mistakes.
- Affects enterprise contract SLA; customer flagged as P1.

Environment:
- prod via edge region us-east -> api-gateway -> nginx-based edge-proxy -> internal route to serving-runtime.
- Customer traffic patterns: long single-turn generations (high prefix + long completion).

Steps to reproduce (observed / suggested):
1) Use the customer prompt used in their repro bundle (attached) that reliably produces ~2200 tokens completion.
2) Open SSE connection to /v1/stream with keepalive enabled and accept chunked transfer encoding.
3) Observe a successful stream most times; intermittently the client receives everything except the final 1-3 sentences and no terminal 'done' event.

Repro notes:
- Repro increases when artificially delaying client reads (simulate slow consumer) and when packetization coalescing at the edge is enabled.
- Repro is NOT observed when bypassing the edge-proxy (direct node -> serving-runtime) in our staging environment.

Initial logs / traces attached:
- request ids: req-us-12345-mln, req-us-12378-mln (examples where final segment missing).
- edge access logs show 200 and normal Content-Type but edge metrics show 'finish_write' occurred before final chunk flushed to downstream in ~60% of repro cases.

Suggested urgency: P1 / Sev1 because enterprise customer and SLA risk.
comments: Support (Maya): Initial triage with customer produced sample request bundle and capture from their client (client includes headers + raw bytes). Customer confirms bypassing corporate proxy reduces occurrence.
SRE (Anika): I can see correlated spikes in edge write latency for the request ids. Opening a packet capture next. Assigned to Arjun for deeper tracing into edge config.
Customer (BrightCart Eng): We can reproduce locally with our mobile emulator when the connection enters a slow-start (cellular) profile. Happily provided curl traces and chrome net internals dumps.

Engineering (Arjun): Running targeted repro in staging with edge-proxy in front of serving-runtime. Observed chunk coalescing in nginx buffers where final '\n' terminator became coalesced with keepalive probe and downstream client parsed stream as closed without final event. Working on further instrumentation.

SRE (Anika): Added temporary log to edge layer to emit flush timestamps and chunk boundary markers. We saw multiple cases where the last data write had a timestamp equal to the keepalive write and downstream connection closed shortly after.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Edge proxy (nginx) buffer coalescing + keepalive/fast-finish race causes final data chunk to be merged with a zero-length or keepalive write that a client or CDN interprets as end-of-stream, dropping the terminal metadata.

What we ran:
- Reproduced with instrumented edge in staging: toggled proxy sendfile/chunked_transfer and proxy_buffering flags. Disabling proxy_buffering reduced failures from ~0.5% -> ~0.01% for the test set.
- Verified that direct bypass of edge (same serving-runtime) shows no failures.
- Captured tcpdump: last small packet often contained only keepalive frames and then an RST from an intermediate NAT (customer corp NAT) in some cases.
- Correlated with client-side slow-consumer behavior: slower read windows cause nginx to buffer more aggressively and coalesce writes when connection resumes.

Related signals / links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/edge-write-latency (pan to 2026-03-10 15:00 - 17:00)
- Slack thread: #support BrightCart / messages: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234ABC/p1641212345678
- Packet captures attached in Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/SUPPORT/edge-slowstart-packets

Preliminary root cause: Combined behavior of nginx proxy_buffering + edge keepalive writes can cause final application chunk to be combined with a keepalive/zero-length probe which some intermediate network elements (corporate NATs, CDNs) treat as a connection-stealing probe, resulting in the final terminal-data never being delivered to the client. The serving-runtime did emit the final tokens and terminal event; loss is happening between edge and client.

Next steps (in progress):
- Deploy temporary mitigation in prod us-east: set proxy_buffering off and reduce proxy_send_timeout for customer route.
- Implement additional guard in serving-runtime to emit an explicit final terminator event (unique token) before closing the stream so downstream coalescing won't hide terminal metadata.
- Create an edge-safe flushing PR to ensure last chunk is flushed as its own packet when stream is ending.
resolution: Mitigation in place: prod us-east edge route updated to disable nginx proxy_buffering for BrightCart routes and proxy_send_timeout reduced. Serving-runtime patched to emit explicit terminal event token prior to stream close and PR created to make this behavior configurable. These mitigations reduced observed failure rate in canary to <0.02% for the test traffic.
resolution_notes:
Fix summary:
- Short-term: Disabled proxy_buffering + tuned timeouts for target route (rolled 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC).
- Medium-term: Serving-runtime change (PR #907) to append explicit '\n--END-STREAM-TERMINATOR--\n' marker before closing stream (configurable via 'stream.terminator_token'). Deployed to canary and then to us-east.
- Long-term: Edge-proxy PR #1423 adds an option to force last-chunk-flush (sets tcp_nodelay and flush after final send) and monitoring alert to catch increase in edge coalescing metrics.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Postmortem doc + customer-facing incident summary to be drafted by CS (Maya) by 2026-03-14.
- Runbook update to include proxy_buffering checklist for streaming workloads (owner: Anika).
- Instrumentation: add metric edge.final_chunk_coalesce_rate (owner: Observability team).

Customer communication:
- Notified BrightCart of interim mitigation and asked them to validate on their end. They confirmed reduced occurrence in their QA fleet. Next: schedule joint verification window 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC.

Status: In Progress — mitigations deployed to production us-east; monitoring in place; preparing full rollout and postmortem.
